_comment: Neutral hook registration. ai-sync renders this into ~/.claude/settings.json (Claude schema), ~/.cursor/hooks.json (Cursor schema), and ~/.copilot/hooks/ai-wow.json (Copilot schema). 'script' resolves to each tool's hooks/ dir ('copilot' points straight at this repo's hooks/ — see bin/ai-sync _cmd_for); 'command' is raw (BIN/ -> this repo's bin/).
_copilot_caveat: VERIFIED LIVE against Copilot CLI 1.0.80 (2026-08-21). Copilot runs two hook contracts and the event-name CASING picks which: camelCase (preToolUse) gets Copilot's native shape — payload {sessionId,toolName,toolArgs} where toolArgs is a JSON *string*, reply with top-level permissionDecision. PascalCase (PreToolUse), which ai-sync renders, gets the Claude-compatible shape on BOTH sides — payload {hook_event_name,session_id,tool_name,tool_input:{command}}, reply with nested hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision. So these scripts work under Copilot unchanged; keep the PascalCase rendering. Confirmed: PreToolUse fires and blocks (guard-destructive denied a real command); Stop fires; the docs' required 'version: 1' is NOT needed (hooks load without it); 'ask' becomes deny when the run is non-interactive; a {} reply is accepted as no-opinion. SubagentStart and SubagentStop also fire — but the casing compat is per-event, not global: those two deliver Copilot's NATIVE camelCase payload ({sessionId,timestamp,cwd,transcriptPath}) even under a PascalCase key, with no tool_input. stamp-tracker reads tool_input.subagent_type/prompt, so the stamp-tracker-spawn mapping is inert under Copilot — it runs and exits 0, but the payload simply does not carry the fields it needs, so this is not fixable by renaming keys.
